tasks.title: Drag and drop widgets into and out of a Stack widget
tasks.description:
Bug: in the dashboard editor, widgets can't be dragged into or out of a Stack widget. Dragging an existing widget (e.g. Market) over a Stack doesn't drop it into the stack (the grid only shows the 12-column row placement), and a stack's children can't be dragged back out onto the row. Today children can only be added via the stack's own '+ Add' button.

Decided: dragging out places the child at the guide column with width 6 (or the free span from firstFreeSpan); block the drop when fitsInRow fails, like rows do.
Decided: dropping into a stack inserts at the hovered index; the child's column is dropped (width is driven by the stack).
Decided: a stack cannot be dropped into a stack (no nesting), consistent with exclude=['stack'] in the stack's add dialog.

[next-iteration 2026-11-27]
Answer (breaking changes): "Allowed".
Decided: dragged-out child width = min(6, 12 - totalSpan(row)); block only when the row is full; the guide shows the shrunken span - matches cross-row move packing (insertByColumn + clampRowToLine) and addWidget shrinking.
Decided: the stack drop zone wins only while the pointer is over the stack card's body (children area); its header and surrounding gaps keep targeting the row guide.
Decided: a child dropped into a stack gets width = stack width and no column, mirroring addChild (stack/Widget.vue:56).
Note: row drag session is module-level in DashboardRow.vue and never mutates lists; needs a shared drag-session lib with stack drop zones and one atomic row<->stack update in DashboardEditView.

[next-iteration 2026-11-27]
Plan: /tmp/delivery-Mtft/stack-drag-and-drop.md. Decided (plan gate): zone = the card's whole .widget-body; same drag-out rule in every row; keyboard path into/out of a stack deferred (recorded as debt in docs/agents/features.md - rows have no keyboard cross-row move either); empty stack hover = dashed placeholder + marker at 0; all drops incl. same-row go through one WIDGET_MOVE handler.

Decided: unticking hides the Dark tab and keeps the values, no confirm dialog - the backend keeps dormant dark data, so nothing is destroyed and re-ticking restores it.

tasks.title: Theme backgrounds: separate background parameters for dark mode
tasks.description:
Background settings (gradients, image, etc.) become per-mode parameters: dark mode gets its own background values instead of sharing the light ones. Backend theme model, CSS generation and editor all need the new dark background fields.

[qualify-sprint 2026-11-27]
Size: complex
Scope: Restructure the stored theme into background: {light: {gradient: {direction, stops}, image: {ref, fit, position, repeat}}, dark: {...}} (mirrors colors.light/dark) and add an explicit darkMode bool to Theme and Meta. This task owns the whole schema change and the rendering of the flag. Files: internal/themes types.go (validation: dark palette required only when darkMode), store.go (readThemeFile decodes the legacy shape through a legacy struct and converts it; plain json.Unmarshal would silently drop old keys), css.go (one bgFor(mode), no per-field fallback; Palette/background return light for every colorMode when darkMode is false; Meta.PreviewCSS too), builtins default and ember (darkMode true), testdata/theme_css_fixture.json, webui/src/types/theme.ts and webui/src/lib/themeCss.ts (mirror). Editor fields are wired in task 53. Precondition: the uncommitted shared-image-pool removal in the working tree (asset: becomes the only ref scheme) is committed before this starts. Update docs/agents/viewer.md (Editing a background) and docs/agents/features.md. Acceptance: new Go and TS fixture cases pass (dark-only gradient, different dark fit, light image with plain dark, darkMode off gives identical light and dark rules); a migration test loads a legacy theme with background.image.light and no darkMode key (the Banana case) and gets darkMode true with the light background copied into dark.
Depends on: none
Breaking changes: allowed (theme.json shape and the GET/PUT /themes API body change; old files are migrated on load and rewritten on next save; older binaries would drop backgrounds)
Decided: explicit darkMode bool, not implicit presence of dark data - zero value matches light-only by default and lets dark data stay stored while off.
Decided: themes without the darkMode key load with darkMode true, builtins set it in code - defaulting off would silently turn existing dark dashboards light.
Decided: an empty dark background renders the plain dark palette, no fallback to light - the task asks for its own values instead of sharing; the migration copies the light background into dark so today's rendering is kept.
Decided: turning dark mode off keeps the dark colours, background and file stored but unused - reversible, no data loss on an accidental click.
Decided: with darkMode off every colorMode renders the light palette and background - a light-only theme has nothing else to show.
Decided: light and dark may reference the same file - lets the migration copy the light ref without duplicating files.
Answer: "Restructure, allow break (Recommended)"

tasks.title: Theme backgrounds: only one background file per mode
tasks.description:
A theme allows at most one background image file per mode: one for light and, if dark mode is enabled, one for dark.

[qualify-sprint 2026-11-27]
Size: medium
Scope: References already allow one image per mode (light.image.ref, dark.image.ref from task 56); enforce the rule in storage: themes Store.Update deletes every file in the theme assets/ folder that neither light.image.ref nor dark.image.ref references (a dark ref kept while darkMode is off still counts). Keep the existing upload endpoint and content-addressed/uploaded names, no fixed names and no new endpoint. Pruning happens on save only, never on load or startup. Files: internal/themes/store.go (+ store_test.go), app/router/handlers/themes.go if needed, webui useThemeAssets if its contract changes. The per-mode upload slot in the editor is built in task 53. Acceptance: Go store test - upload two light images, save referencing the second: exactly one file remains; a file referenced by dark survives; a theme with extra legacy files keeps them after load and loses them after the next save.
Depends on: 78xtfae (task 56)
Breaking changes: allowed (unreferenced files in existing themes are deleted on their next save)
Decided: storage enforces the rule by pruning unreferenced assets on save, not fixed file names - overwriting a stable URL leaves stale browser and render caches and needs a new endpoint; editor-only enforcement lets the folder fill up again.
Decided: light and dark may reference the same file - pruning just counts references.
Decided: an image behind a gradient stays allowed as today - the task does not ask to change it.
Answer: "Prune on save (Recommended)"

[next-iteration 2026-11-27]
Decided: prune on save skips files modified in the last 5 minutes (grace window) - an edit made during an upload can start a save with the old ref; the grace window keeps the just-uploaded file; orphans go on a later save. 5 minutes is a small choice.
Decided: the editor awaits any pending autosave before uploading, then sets the ref and saves immediately (built with task 53).
